title: Strict Roos comparison and integral completeness across a finite clopen cover
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions].

Write $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $r_i$ for restriction of its module sheaves and complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A strict tower consists of complexes $C_n$ and chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$, with morphisms the compatible families of chain maps. Restriction and sectionwise product gluing are inverse equivalences on these strict towers. Restriction identifies termwise countable products with the component products, carries the endomorphism $(c_n)_n\mapsto(c_n-t_n(c_{n+1}))_n$ to the identical component formula, and induces a natural chain isomorphism
$$r_i\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_C)[-1]\cong\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_{r_iC})[-1].$$
This comparison is compatible with strict tower maps and their projections. On derived categories it preserves the derived-limit property, with its specified Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. In particular the actual reduction maps $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ and the transitions restrict to the corresponding component maps [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower].

Derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete] is equivalent to derived completeness of every component, retaining the specified first map to the product in the Roos triangle. Membership in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] is equivalent to componentwise membership. Membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] is likewise equivalent to componentwise membership. For both the cohomological supports of all positive reductions and their Tor amplitudes, any common bounds for the finite list of component bounds uniform in $n$ are uniform bounds on $X$.

The unbounded restriction equivalence therefore restricts to these two integral full subcategories. It preserves completed tensor products and their coefficient units as defined by the strict reduction towers in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For every finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L$, it commutes naturally with the integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], including the level maps to $A_{L,m}$ and their transitions. No canonical cone is asserted in a bare triangulated category: functoriality refers to the displayed strict complex model. All assertions include the empty partition.

proof.text: Use the unchanged canonical coefficient and restriction definitions extracted to [def-pur-clopen-integral-restriction]. The completed coefficient comparison is uniquely normalized by all finite quotient projections, so transporting along it changes neither restriction nor its reduction maps. Its scalar-restriction equivalence and preservation of countable products give the hypotheses of the generic signed Roos comparison. Apply comparison_iso, comparison_transition_generic, comparison_iso_coordinates and comparison_iso_evaluation to this exact additive restriction. This proves the strict Roos comparison with both signed cone coordinates and every evaluation map.

For strict tower gluing retain the recorded plan: apply [lem-pur-clopen-strict-tower-roos-equivalence] to the completed coefficient ring and transport each component along the unique completed coefficient isomorphism. For derived Roos descent apply integralRoosCalculus of [lem-pur-clopen-augmented-integral-descent], whose exact module equivalence and countable-product comparison preserve and reflect the specified distinguished triangle with its first and last maps.

proof.text: Apply augmentedIntegralReductionComparison from [lem-pur-clopen-augmented-integral-descent] and take its augmented-reduction conjunct. Apply augmentedIntegralMembershipBounds and take its completeness, integral constructibility, finite-Tor constructibility, fixed-interval support and fixed-interval Tor conjuncts. These are exactly the assertions finiteClopen_augmented_reduction and finiteClopen_integral_membership. The resolution-reduction assertion retains its recorded proof plan using the same augmented comparison on restricted K-flat resolutions. For the remaining resolution clause, use K-flat preservation from [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], then compare an arbitrary K-flat resolution with a flat-term K-flat resolution by the canonical reduction-tower comparison.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1(1) and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24. Agent finite-clopen augmented reduction and uniform-bound application, returned proof steps 5-7.

proof.text: Take the unbounded equivalence from the derived Roos descent assertion. By the integral membership equivalences of step 3, its restriction and inverse carry exactly the objects of each integral full subcategory. Define both restricted functors on the same underlying morphisms. Lift the ambient unit and counit to the full subcategories; membership of inverse images follows by invariance under the counit isomorphism. The forgetful squares are definitionally identical, so their natural isomorphisms are identity maps. For finite-Tor membership, transport each reduced test presentation along the coefficient reduction of the ambient isomorphism. This works for the empty family as well.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1(1) and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24. Agent finite-clopen augmented reduction and uniform-bound application, returned proof steps 5-7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-completed-operation-towers] to $M,N$ and to each $E\subset L$. Its natural derived isomorphisms identify the strict-model completed tensor, coefficient units and scalar extension; the specified pure-tensor maps retain every finite-level map and transition. The isomorphisms are induced by strict cone comparisons, so this asserts precisely strict-model functoriality. Each of the three cited clopen results includes the empty partition; step 2 then supplies $[0,0]$ if no component supplies an interval, and all displayed maps are zero in the zero categories.
